newsitem.title: USA: Tobacco tax may not go for child health - senators.
newsitem.headline: Tobacco tax may not go for child health - senators.

text.p: Leading Congressional backers of raising tobacco taxes said they are outraged by a Republican proposal to raise the tax but not dedicate any of the revenue to expand child health care coverage.

Senator Orrin Hatch of Utah and Rep. Nancy Johnson of Connecticut, both Republicans, and Sen. Edward Kennedy of Massachusetts, a Democrat, told a news conference that although the tax plan is still in flux, it appears that the latest Republican proposal is to raise cigarette taxes but not use the money for the intended purpose of expanding health care for children.

The conservative-liberal team of Hatch and Kennedy managed to get overwhelming support in the Senate for their plan to raise cigarette taxes by 20 cents and use the money for health insurance for children of the working poor. They said the added cost of cigarettes would also discourage teenage smoking.

Johnson released an angry letter she sent to House Speaker Newt Gingrich and other House leaders. She said it was "outrageous" and out of step with rank-and-file Republicans to keep the tax but not use it for child health.

"How in the world can they keep the 20 cents in there and not take care of the kids. To me, that's unbelievable," said Hatch. The Hatch-Kennedy proposal would use $8 billion of the money raised by the tobacco tax for health care.

"It's time for people to stop playing games with children," said Hatch, who added he would have to "reassess" whether he could support the overall spending bill if it does not include that money for the children's health.
Kennedy said, "We know where the country stands.. Where does Congress stand? With Big Tobacco or little children."

Noting that $8 billion is a tiny amount in a multi-trillion dollar budget, Hatch said if he does not succeed in winning children's coverage this time around he'll try again and "If we come back at it, it won't be for 8 billion bucks."
